title: Flame Wall Guide — Projectile Added Damage, Ignite, Wall Limits and Infusion
summary: Flame Wall creates one or more walls of fire. Projectiles that pass through a wall gain added Fire Damage, and enemies in the wall can be Ignited. It is a strong support layer for fire and projectile builds, and for minion projectile builds. This guide covers wall direction, ignite, wall limits, Lightning Infusion consumption and boss placement.
description: Flame Wall deep guide: what the wall does, projectile added damage on pass-through, ignite behaviour, which projectiles count, multiple walls and the fourth-wall limit, Circular Wall Support, Lightning Infusion consumption, ignite ground questions, mapping and boss placement, minion usage, troubleshooting and community questions.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial
imageAlt: Flame Wall fire spell skill icon

sections.title: Quick Answer
paragraphs: Flame Wall itself deals some Fire Damage and Ignites enemies standing in it, but its main value is that projectiles passing through the wall gain added Fire Damage.
The projectile must travel from one side of the wall to the other — shooting from behind the wall through it into the enemy is what grants the bonus.
You can have a limited number of walls; casting a fourth removes the oldest. Circular Wall Support changes the wall shape.

sections.title: Requirements
paragraphs: No special attribute gate. Flame Wall is a spell gem; it works with any build that fires projectiles through the wall.

sections.title: Wall Projectile Empowerment
paragraphs: When a projectile crosses the wall, it gains added Fire Damage for that pass. The bonus applies to player, minion, totem and ally projectiles that actually travel through the wall from one side to the other.
A projectile that spawns beyond the wall, or that only clips the edge without crossing, does not get the bonus — the pass-through is what matters.
This makes positioning the wall between you and the enemy the key skill: you want your projectiles to cross it before they hit.
bullets: Player, minion, totem, ally projectiles all count.
Must cross from one side to the other.
Spawned-beyond-wall projectiles do not benefit.

sections.title: Ignite Behaviour
paragraphs: Enemies standing in the wall can be Ignited by the wall's own Fire Damage. The wall also can let your projectiles carry Ignite if your build ignites on hit.
The wall itself is not Ignited Ground by default; the ignite comes from the wall's damage or your projectiles, not from the ground beneath the wall.
Flame Wall can still make projectiles apply Ignite if your other gear or supports cause ignite on hit.
bullets: Wall ignites enemies inside it.
Wall is not Ignited Ground by itself.
Projectiles can carry Ignite from your build.

sections.title: Infusion Mode
paragraphs: Lightning Infusion can be consumed by Flame Wall to add Lightning to the wall's damage, then the infusion is spent on that hit.
The added Lightning applies to the wall and to projectiles passing through if the infusion is active when they cross.
Because infusion is consumed, you need a steady infusion source to keep Lightning Flame Wall running.
bullets: Lightning Infusion adds Lightning, then is consumed.
Projectiles crossing during infusion get the bonus.
Needs an infusion source to sustain.

sections.title: Skill Interactions
paragraphs: Flame Wall layers with Spark, Oil Grenade and other fire or projectile skills: drop the wall, then fire through it.
For minion builds, place the wall so minion projectiles cross it; the bonus applies to ally projectiles as well.
Eye of Winter and other spell projectiles also gain the added Fire when they pass through.
bullets: Pairs with Spark and Oil Grenade.
Minion projectiles crossing get the bonus.
Spell projectiles like Eye of Winter count.

sections.title: Support Compatibility
paragraphs: Flame Wall is a spell, so spell damage, area, duration and fire supports apply. Increased Duration keeps walls up longer; fire and ignite supports raise the wall's own damage.
bullets: Increased Duration for longer walls.
Fire and Ignite supports for wall damage.
Area supports widen the wall.

sections.title: Support Loadouts
paragraphs: A utility Flame Wall uses duration and area supports. A fire-build variant adds ignite and fire-penetration supports for the wall's own damage.
bullets: Utility: Increased Duration, Area, Spell Damage.
Fire: Ignite, Fire Penetration, Burning Damage.
Circular Wall Support changes the shape.

sections.title: Mapping Rotation
paragraphs: In maps, drop the wall just in front of the pack so your projectiles cross it into the enemies. Keep moving and re-drop as you advance.
Because you can only hold a few walls, treat it as a per-pack buff rather than a permanent field.
bullets: Wall in front of the pack, fire through.
Re-drop as you move.
Limited walls: use per pack.

sections.title: Bossing Rotation
paragraphs: Against a boss, place the wall between you and the boss so every projectile crosses it. Refresh the wall during downtimes so it does not expire mid-fight.
If the boss moves past the wall, reposition it; the bonus only applies while projectiles cross.
bullets: Wall between you and boss.
Refresh during downtimes.
Reposition if boss crosses the wall.

sections.title: Minion Usage
paragraphs: Minion projectile builds benefit a lot: place the wall so minion projectiles cross it, and the added Fire applies to every minion shot.
This is a cheap way to add a damage layer to a minion army without extra gem sockets on the minions themselves.
bullets: Minion projectiles crossing get added Fire.
Cheap damage layer for minion builds.
Position wall on the minion firing line.

sections.title: Build Usage
paragraphs: Flame Wall fits fire and projectile builds, including Fire Smith of Kitava and minion projectile setups, as a support layer rather than a main damage skill.
It is a low-tier gem, so it is easy to slot into league-start fire builds.
bullets: Fire Bear Smith of Kitava: fire layer.
Minion projectile builds: ally-projectile bonus.
League-start fire builds: easy slot.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: If projectiles look like they cross the wall but gain no damage, you are likely firing from the wrong side or the projectile spawned beyond the wall. Stand so the wall is between you and the enemy.
If walls keep disappearing, you are over the limit; let the oldest expire or stop recasting.
bullets: No bonus: wrong side or spawned beyond wall.
Walls vanish: over the limit, stop recasting.
No ignite: wall ignites, not ignite-ground.
Weak wall: add fire and ignite supports.
Infusion gone: need a steady source.

sections.title: Community Evidence
paragraphs: Flame Wall is frequently recommended as a projectile damage layer in fire build threads, especially for minion projectile armies.
The common confusion is wall direction: players report 'no bonus' until they learn to fire through the wall.
bullets: Recommended as a projectile damage layer.
Wall-direction confusion is the top question.
